annotations.title: Repenting him.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Note how spedily the plague of God falleth after sinne, and specially men must note what torment of conscience, and desperation often foloweth the sheading of innocent bloud.

annotations.title: Hung him self.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> If he had rightly repented, notwithstanding his horrible treason, he might haue obteyned mercy: but by hanging him self he tooke away al meanes of mercy and saluation, because he died finally impenitent.

annotations.title: Innocent of his bloud.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Though Pilate was much more innocent then the Iewes, and would haue been free from the murder of our Sauiour, seeking al the meanes that he could (without offending the people and the Emperours lawes) to dimisse him: Yet he is damned for being the minister of the peoples wicked wil against his owne conscience. euen as al Officers be, and specially the Iudges and Iuries which execute lawes of temporal Princes against Catholike men: for al such be guilty of innocent bloud, and be nothing excused by that they execute other mens will according to the lawes, which be vniust. For they should rather suffer death them selues, then put an innocent man to death.

notes.text: They that execute lawes against their conscience, are like to Pilate.

annotations.title: If thou be the Sonne.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Maruel not, when thou hearest our Sauiour in the B. Sacrament mocked at, or seest him abused of wicked men, that he straight reuengeth not such blasphemies: or that he sheweth not him self there visibly and to the senses, when faithles Heretikes wil say, Let me see him, tast him, &c. for he suffered here the like on the Crosse, when he might at his will haue come downe with as much ease as he rose when he was dead.

notes.text: Christ derided in the B. Sacrament, euen as vpon the Crosse.

annotations.title: Why hast thou forsaken me.
annotations.text: Beware here of the detestable blasphemie of Caluin and the Caluinists, [1]who thinking not the bodily death of Christ sufficient, say, that he was also here so forsaken and abandoned of his Father, that he sustained in soule and conscience the very feares and torments of the damned. And to take away the Article of his descending into Hel after his death, (which was [2]with triumph and not in paine,) they say that his descending was nothing els, but that his soule suffered the very paines of Hel vpon the Crosse. Whereas in deede by these wordes out of the Psalme, our Sauiour wil signifie no more but that his paines (being now so long on the Crosse and ready to die) were very great, and therfore according to the infirmity of his humane nature, for very anguish (as before in the garden when he was but toward his Passion) he saith he was forsaken, for two causes, first because it was the wil of God not to deliuer him, but that he should die: secondly, because his diuine nature did so represse it self for the time, that he felt no comfort thereof at al, but was left to die in extreme paines as a mere man.

notes.text: Detestable blasphemy of Calvin. And other Ministers of his school.

annotations.title: Wrapped.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> This honour and duty done to Christes body being dead, was maruelous grateful and meritorious. And this wrapping of it in cleane sindon may signifie by S. Hierom, <mn>[2]</mn>that the Body of our Lord is to be wrapped not in gold, pretious stones, and silke, but in pure linnen. And so in the whole Church it is obserued by <mn>[3]</mn> S. Siluesters constitution, that the Corporal <mn>[4]</mn> whereupon our Lordes body lieth on the altar, must be pure and plaine linnen.

notes.text: Reuerent vsing of our L. Body.
